Heard Sri Arun Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Nikhil Singh, learned Additional Government Advocate-I for the State.

2. By means of present anticipatory bail application, the applicant has shown his apprehension of arrest in Case Crime No. 0270 of 2023 u/s 120B, 498A, 323, 506, 504, 376D, 354, 392, 342 IPC &
3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Motigarpur, District Sultanpur.

It has been submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence alleged in the F.I.R.

sentences.text: Now the chargesheet has been filed and the present applicant who is mother-in-law of the victim has cooperated in the investigation and she did not misuse the liberty which was protected by the Division Bench.
Learned counsel has stated that the present applicant shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of anticipatory bail, if granted.

Further attention has been drawn towards Annexure no. 11 which is a bail order dated 13.6.2024 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 5428 of 2024 (Karan Pandey vs. State of U.P.) granted bail to the husband of the victim / son of the present applicant.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer of learned counsel for the applicant but could not dispute the submissions of learned counsel for the applicant.

5. Without entering into the merits of the issue and cconsidering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, contents and allegations of the F.I.R., the undertaking of the applicant that he shall cooperate with the trial proceedings, it would be expedient in the interest of justice that the liberty of the applicant may be protected till conclusion of trial in view of dictum of Apex Court in re:
